items.q: What makes a medicine high alert?
o: Small errors cause serious harm, so extra checks, standard concentrations and monitoring are built in
It is expensive to buy
It is rarely prescribed
It has a pleasant taste
items.exp: High alert status follows harm from error, not price or frequency. Insulin, anticoagulants, concentrated electrolytes and opioids need engineered safeguards (ISMP). No milligram doses are taught here; ward charts govern them.
r: Correct: Recognise high alert medicines.
Price does not predict error harm.
Rare use raises, not lowers, risk.
Taste is irrelevant to systemic harm.

A month of stopping invites thrombosis.
Hidden continuation risks operative bleeding.
Supplements do not reverse modern anticoagulants.
